title: Validate Binary Search Tree
statement: Given a binary tree as a level-order list `root`, return `true` if it is a valid binary search tree: every node's left subtree holds only values strictly less than the node, and every right subtree holds only values strictly greater. Duplicate values make the tree invalid.

predict_steps.prompt: At node 4 under root 5, what upper bound must 4 respect?
predict_steps.answer: 5 (strictly less than ancestor 5 on the right path)
predict_steps.hint: Right child of 5 must be > 5; 4 fails immediately.

predict_steps.prompt: Even if 4 were 7, would node 3 (left of 4) be valid under root 5?
predict_steps.hint: Deep nodes must still obey ancestor bounds.

viva.question: How do bounds (low, high) validate a BST in O(n)?
What fails if you only compare a node to its direct children?
Why are the allowed ranges open at the node’s value?
expected_points: BST forbids duplicates or strict inequality
